title: RBAC v2 PRD + success metrics for enterprise controls (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
creator: Naomi Feldman
description:
Context / problem
Regulated enterprise customers evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Private have made least-privilege authorization and evidence-grade auditability gating requirements. RBAC v1 is currently too coarse and inconsistently enforced across the API Gateway, Control Plane services, and Console/admin tooling.

This ticket owns the PRD for RBAC v2 and the definition of success metrics and rollout gates. It is the “source of truth” for Product alignment across Security/Compliance, Platform, Console, and Private Deployments.

Goals
1) Define the customer problem and required capabilities for enterprise adoption (Dedicated + Private, plus Hosted where applicable).
2) Specify RBAC v2 product requirements: primitives, scope semantics, workflows, and operator UX.
3) Define measurable success metrics + guardrails for rollout (deny rate, support ticket volume, adoption of templates, coverage).
4) Align phased release plan with enterprise roadmap and pilot customer needs.

Non-goals (RBAC v2)
- Customer-exposed ABAC / policy scripting language.
- Full identity re-architecture (SSO/SAML integration continues; RBAC is authorization layer).
- Replacing all internal admin tooling in one release (we’ll stage Console UI vs API-only workflows).

Personas
- Security Admin (enterprise): wants least-privilege roles, separation of duties (SoD), auditability, and clear break-glass controls.
- Platform Operator (enterprise): manages deployments, routing policies, model rollouts; needs predictable access and troubleshooting.
- Auditor / Compliance (enterprise): read-only visibility into org/deployment configuration + audit exports with decision context.
- Redwood Support/Solutions Engineer: needs “why denied?” guidance, safe debugging, and consistent remediation steps.

User stories (high priority)
A. As a Security Admin, I can assign built-in role templates (Org Admin / Security Admin / Billing Admin / Read-only Auditor / Deployment Operator) scoped to an org, project, environment, or cluster (Private), and verify what each role can do.
B. As a Platform Operator, I can update routing policies/model pinning/rollout configurations only in the environments I operate, without being able to manage users, billing, or security settings.
C. As an Auditor, I can view audit logs and export them to a SIEM, but cannot modify any settings or access secrets.
D. As an admin, when I’m denied, I can see actionable “denied because…” info (permission missing / wrong scope / policy version) and how to request access.
E. As Security/Compliance, I can produce evidence for SOC2/customer questionnaires: permission catalog, enforcement coverage, authorization decision logging, and break-glass procedures.

Functional requirements (MVP)
1) Permission catalog + classification
- Canonical permission strings with namespacing and versioning rules (per ADR-014).
- Inventory coverage across security-relevant actions in Hosted API, Console, Control Plane, Dedicated + Private admin operations.
- Sensitivity tiers for actions (e.g., secrets/key mgmt vs read-only vs deployment operations).

2) RBAC primitives + scope semantics
- Entities: permission, role (collection of permissions), role binding (subject->role at scope).
- Scopes: org (required), and at least one lower scope (project/environment) for Dedicated/Hosted; plus cluster scope for Private (installer/admin workflows).
- Deny-by-default: endpoints must be explicitly annotated or checked; missing annotation = deny.
- Compatibility strategy: dual-read/feature-flagged migration from RBAC v1.

3) Consistent enforcement + error semantics
- Enforce at gateway with service-side verification for critical ops (per ADR-015 and API standards).
- Standardized errors (HTTP 403 + structured reason codes). Avoid leaking sensitive permissions to non-admin users.
- Optional debug header / admin-only detail for Support/SecOps workflows.

4) Auditability
- Audit events include authorization decision context: subject, action, scope, decision allow/deny, policy version, denial reason code.
- Audit export includes authz context in SIEM-friendly mapping.

5) Console/operator UX (MVP)
- View role bindings for an org + drill down by scope.
- Apply role templates and assign to users/groups.
- Permission viewer/search (read-only) and role template descriptions.
- “Why was I denied?” UX: link to request access and show minimal actionable hints.

Out of scope for MVP (explicit)
- Custom role editor for arbitrary roles (we may ship templates first; editor can follow).
- Cross-org delegation / reseller multi-tenant admin.

Key workflows to validate end-to-end (definition of done for MVP)
- Manage API keys: create/rotate/revoke keys (Hosted + Dedicated) with correct scoping.
- Modify routing policies and rollout configs: only Deployment Operator or Org Admin at correct scope.
- Export audit logs: Auditor can export; non-auditor cannot.
- Manage org/users/roles: Security Admin/Org Admin only.
- Private installer bootstrap: initial admin binding + IdP group mapping + safe recovery.

Success metrics (ship + 30/60/90 day)
We will track metrics at two levels: (1) safety/quality during rollout, and (2) enterprise value/adoption.

A) Rollout safety / quality metrics (leading indicators)
1. Authorization deny rate (by endpoint + by customer tier)
- Target: no sustained p95 deny rate increase > +0.5% on “expected allow” endpoints during pilot (measured in dual-read mode vs v1 baseline).
- Guardrail: if deny rate spikes > 2% absolute on a critical workflow (key rotation, routing edits, audit export) for >30 minutes, auto-alert + rollback checklist.

2. Authz check latency overhead
- Target: added overhead p95 < 5ms at gateway; p99 < 15ms (measured per region).
- Guardrail: any endpoint exceeding p95 +10ms attributable to authz caching/regressions requires perf review before broad enablement.

3. Coverage / annotation completeness
- Target: 100% of endpoints in the “sensitive actions” inventory have explicit permission annotations/checks before GA.
- CI gate: fail builds if new sensitive endpoints are introduced without annotations (owned by Eng, but measured here).

4. Regression and bypass detection
- Target: 0 known bypasses at GA; all bypass incidents must result in regression tests and postmortem notes (tie to incident on streaming route hotfix).

B) Enterprise value / adoption metrics (lagging indicators)
1. Template adoption
- Target: >= 70% of enterprise orgs (Dedicated/Private) use at least one built-in role template within 60 days of enablement.

2. Support burden
- Target: “permission denied after migration” tickets per 10 enterprise accounts <= 1.0/week after first 2 weeks of rollout.
- Breakdown: (a) missing permissions in templates, (b) wrong scope binding, (c) product bugs, (d) customer misunderstanding.

3. Customer success milestones
- Target: unblock at least 2 enterprise pilots (1 Private, 1 Dedicated) that explicitly list least-privilege + audit export as a gate.
- Track: Ironbank Financial, Northbridge Healthcare, Aegis Insurance (pipeline references in HubSpot; see PM-690 for launch readiness).

4. Compliance evidence readiness
- Target: publish “RBAC v2 evidence pack” internally (permission catalog snapshot + design docs + test coverage + audit log schema) within 30 days of GA.

Instrumentation notes (what we need from Eng)
- Metrics: allow/deny counts by permission, endpoint, and scope type; latency histograms for policy evaluation; cache hit rate; “missing annotation” counts.
- Logs: structured denial reason codes (admin-safe), policy version identifiers.
- Dashboard: rollout dashboard with deny rate, top denial reasons, and top endpoints by deny volume.

Release plan (phased)
Phase 0: Discovery (permission inventory + classification)
- Deliverable: permission catalog draft + endpoint mapping + owners (ENG-18241).

Phase 1: Foundations (enforcement + evaluator + audit schema)
- Gateway deny-by-default middleware (ENG-18277) + control plane annotations (ENG-18305).
- Decision logging schema (ENG-18339).
- Dual-read + feature flags + dashboards (ENG-18388).

Phase 2: Operator UX (Console)
- Role management UI MVP + permission viewer/search + denied UX states (DES-914, DES-927).

Phase 3: Pilots (Dedicated + Private)
- Private bootstrap/admin mapping (ENG-18410).
- Customer pilot readiness & comms (PM-690).

Open questions / decisions needed
1) Scope model MVP: org + environment vs org + project + environment (blocked on PM-661 alignment).
2) Separation of duties: do we require distinct Security Admin vs Org Admin templates by default? (Security wants SoD; Sales wants simplicity.)
3) What denial reasons can be exposed to end users vs only org admins? (Security review needed.)
4) How do we represent “group-based bindings” consistently across Hosted/Dedicated/Private (IdP constraints)?

Risks
- Migration churn: existing customers see unexpected denies due to missing template permissions or wrong default mappings.
- Performance regressions at gateway if caching TTLs/invalidation are wrong.
- Inconsistent scoping between Private cluster operations and Control Plane environment semantics.
- Evidence gap: audit exports missing decision context or policy versioning, increasing questionnaire friction.

Acceptance criteria (for this PM ticket)
- PRD published in Confluence (linked in this ticket) and reviewed by Security (Marcus), Platform (Priya/Ethan/Jordan), Console (Chloe/Tessa), and GRC (Olga/Daniel).
- Metrics definitions agreed and documented (including dashboards/owners) with explicit rollout guardrails.
- Phased release plan aligned with PM-690 launch readiness and pilot selection.

References / links
- Confluence: product-docs/requirements/rbac-v2-prd-enterprise-controls (target doc)
- Confluence: security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/rbac-v2-design-overview
- Confluence: security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/permission-inventory-and-classification
- Confluence: architecture-and-standards/api-standards/authorization-check-patterns
- ADRs: adr-014-permission-naming-and-versioning; adr-015-centralized-policy-evaluation-vs-embedded
- Rollout: eng-platform/runbooks/rbac-v2-rollout-runbook

Next steps
- Finalize scope semantics recommendation in PM-661 and incorporate here.
- Confirm pilot accounts + success criteria in PM-690; reflect as explicit exit criteria for Phase 3.
- Confirm dashboard spec (deny rate, reason codes, latency) with Platform; add owners and target dates.
comments: 2025-02-03 — Marcus Lin: Please make sure the PRD explicitly calls out deny-by-default and the requirement that missing annotations are treated as a security bug. Also add a section on what denial metadata is safe to return to end users vs only org admins.

2025-02-07 — Priya Natarajan: Add a hard performance budget and include cache hit-rate targets. We need to be able to say “authz overhead is negligible” in enterprise reviews; make it measurable and enforceable.

2025-02-11 — Tessa Morgan: For Console MVP we should prioritize templates + assignments + permission viewer. A full custom role editor is high-risk for launch; keep it as a follow-up unless required for pilots.

2025-02-18 — Vivek Kulkarni: Private installer bootstrap needs to be in the PRD as a first-class workflow. Customers will ask “how do we get in the first time and map IdP groups?”—we should define the expected UX and recovery path.

2025-03-04 — Kevin Osei: Add explicit requirement that audit export includes authz decision fields and maps cleanly to SIEM schemas. We’ve had customers ask for denial events too, not just allowed actions.

2025-03-12 — Olga Petrov: For SOC2 evidence we need (1) a permission catalog snapshot, (2) proof of enforcement coverage (tests/CI gate), and (3) audit log examples. Please include an “evidence artifacts” checklist as an output of GA.

2025-03-20 — Naomi Feldman: Updated metrics section to include guardrails and clarified that “deny rate” must be split into expected-deny vs expected-allow baselines in dual-read. Still waiting on PM-661 final decision for scope model wording.
